To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
singlet fission in carbon nanotubes is efficient within the solar energy range and can be enhanced via surface functionalization with chlorine atoms.

(i) Singlet fission process in chiral carbon nano-tubes (CNTs) is highly efficient, (ii) singlet exciton-to-bisexciton decay rates are in the 1014-1014 s-1 range, while biexcitons-to-excitons recombination rates are weak, and (iii) MEG in the CNTs can be enhanced with the surface functionalization.

(1) SF in chiral carbon SWCNTs can lead to efficient MEG; (2) the efficiency of the SF MEG process is strongly influenced by the electronic structure of the SWCNTs; and (3) the efficiency of SF MEG can be controlled via the functionalization of SWCNTs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical investigation of the electronic properties of chiral SWCNT, with the emphasis on singlet fission process.
the theoretical study of SF process in chiral SWCNT and its potential applications in solar energy conversion.
the possibility of using SWCNTs as a platform for efficient MEG.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SF is an efficient process for MEG in chiral SWCNT.
the SF MEG is a promising route to enhance the efficiency of solar energy conversion in SWCNTs.
SF in the chiral nanotubes is an effective mechanism for the MEG in the solar spectrum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SF MEG in chiral SWCNT can be enhanced by tuning the low energy electronic states, which would be a promising approach for the design of high efficiency photovoltaic devices.
the SF process can be used as an efficient MEG channel in the chiral carbon nanomaterials.
the SF process in the (6,n), (10,n) SWCNTs is promising as an efficient MEG channel for the solar energy conversion.

the chiral SWCNs can be used as efficient MEG devices.
